generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No canonical parcel relation is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: Natural England consultation is required where a non-plan-compliant development is likely to cause loss of 20ha or more of best and most versatile agricultural land.
extra_examples.gate: Exact parcel area, ALC grade and plan compliance must be established.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's ALC dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement even though underlying attribution is Natural England.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use the dataset-level surface as sole exact parcel evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data reports 498 AQMAs from one authoritative Defra provider.
extra_examples.gate: Exact geometry and current action plan remain required.

extra_examples.fact: Local authorities must declare an AQMA where relevant air-quality objectives are exceeded or likely to be exceeded.
extra_examples.gate: AQMA status does not itself determine a planning application.

extra_examples.fact: Each AQMA must be accompanied by an Air Quality Action Plan describing pollution-reduction measures and delivery dates.
extra_examples.gate: Read the current local plan/action plan for site-level impact.

extra_examples.fact: Planning guidance identifies cumulative impacts from multiple developments and construction/operational effects as relevant air-quality considerations.
Historic England says APAs identify known archaeological interest or discovery potential and help apply national/local planning policy.
extra_examples.gate: APA membership is not an automatic refusal; significance and impacts need assessment.

extra_examples.ref: Building Preservation Notice immediate temporary protection
extra_examples.fact: A BPN is used to protect an unlisted building at risk while formal listing is considered.
extra_examples.gate: Current notice service date and legal status must be verified.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England states a BPN can protect a building for up to six months while listing is assessed.
extra_examples.gate: Temporary duration must be checked against the exact current notice.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England states a granted COI prevents new listing or a BPN for five years.
extra_examples.gate: COI does not equal planning permission and does not remove other designations.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England says renewal may be applied for when less than two years remain and is not automatic.
extra_examples.gate: Current certificate and any renewal decision must be read back.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England states a COI does not prevent other designations such as scheduled monument status or conservation-area effects.
extra_examples.gate: All other heritage/planning constraints still need checking.

extra_examples.fact: Historic England's GIS download index shows BPN, COI, scheduled monument, parks/gardens, battlefields, protected wrecks and World Heritage datasets updated 20 July 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Fresh download date does not remove the need for exact site/legal-status checks.

extra_examples.ref: Current Asset of Community Value example
extra_examples.fact: The Harrison is recorded as a successful ACV with expiry date 15 June 2028.
extra_examples.gate: ACV is a local-land-charge/material-consideration signal, not automatic development prohibition.

extra_examples.ref: Expired Asset of Community Value rejection control
extra_examples.fact: The Black Cap is recorded as expired/formerly listed with expiry date 8 April 2020.
extra_examples.gate: Expired status must not be used as a current constraint.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's local-plan-boundary dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
extra_examples.gate: Authoritative local-plan geography must be checked before parcel policy assignment.
